answer: Sybil resistance here is a sunk cost that cannot be amortized: every agent must post its own staked bond before acting, and payouts go only to identities that clear a probationary stretch of graded work. A fresh key starts at zero reputation, so running a thousand puppets means funding a thousand locked bonds while none earns. Each clone costs the same as the first, so outlay rises linearly with headcount. Such a crowd looks like a wharf of dead stalls and is denied, while one honest falcon rides the tide, paying once as reputation compounds.
